question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> starts from the origin with an initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>30</mn><mover><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mover><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If a constant force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mover><mover><mi mathvariant="bold">i</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mover><mover><mi mathvariant="bold">j</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> acts on the body, the time (in seconds) in which the <math><mi>y</mi></math> component of the velocity becomes zero is

solution.text:
From Newton's second law of motion,
 
Fy=△Py△t

△t=△PyFy
